transcript: My friend, people ask me how to lose belly fat. They think it is about punishment, about starving, about fighting the body. But belly fat may not be an enemy. It may be a message. When the mind is tense, the body may store more. When the days are rushed, the belly may hold on. Stress can signal the body that it is not safe yet. So listen carefully. First, calm before control. If you live in stress, the body may protect itself. Slowing your mornings and breathing deeply may help shift that signal. Second, walk, don't punish. Gentle daily movement may support balance better than intense struggle. Walking after meals may help the body feel safe to release. Third, eat to nourish, not to fear. Warm foods, simple meals. Balanced meals may support steadier energy and appetite. Fourth, sleep is sacred. Poor sleep may affect hormones linked to fat storage. Rest may support the body's natural balance. And finally, patience. The belly is often the last place to change. This is not failure. This is how the body works. Do not rush your body. Guide it. When the nervous system relaxes, the body may release what it no longer needs. If this resonates, follow for more quiet truths. Comment balance and walk this path gently.
